 BLAST Slam IX is the next S-tier Dota 2 tournament, and not only will it feature the best teams in the world, but it’ll also be played in the new 7.42 patch released days ago. Teams are likely still figuring teams out, so it should be a fun and scrappy event to watch. Let’s take a look at my BLAST Slam IX power rankings to see which teams we should keep an eye on.

 Expect Some Upsets 
 Before diving into the individual teams, let’s remember that patch 7.42 was dropped very recently. It’s a massive patch with lots of changes to the map, objectives, and heroes, so even professional teams are still figuring things out.  
 Image via Dota 2 
 Don’t expect to see teams playing at their full potential, as they might misunderstand a thing or two about the patch, which is completely normal this early on. So, there’s a real possibility some of the lower-ranked teams know something we don’t, which can lead to some unexpected upsets that would be very exciting to see. 
 The Top Three Remain the Same 
 As for the power rankings, you really can’t argue much with the top three. The three Eastern European titans have ruled the scene for months, and the gap between them and everyone else is very wide. 
 So far, Team Yandex, Team Spirit, and PARIVISION were the only teams to win S-tier tournaments in the new season, and they look untouchable. However, a new patch might shake things up. 
 Other Teams With Decent a Shot 
 If we’re looking at rosters behind the big three, there are several that look like they can put up a good fight. 
 Aurora clearly look like the number four team in the world. They would always beat teams ranked lower than them, but just can’t crack the top three.  Meanwhile, LGD Gaming seem like they’re always good for a deep run, consistently making it to at least the top six with their new roster. 
 Image via Igor Bezborodov for BLAST 
 Team Liquid was pretty disappointing in their 1win Essence III run where they bombed out in groups , but I still believe in this lineup. We also have GamerLegion – a squad that has really impressed me in the new season. They’ve made it to the playoffs of every single event they’ve competed in post-TI15, so I think it’s fair to put them in the upper half of the tournament.  
 The Rest of the Field 
 Apart from the teams mentioned earlier, I don’t really see anyone else close to contending for the BLAST Slam IX title. However, I’ll point out some underdog squads that I believe have a chance at dealing some damage. 
 Natus Vincere have looked pretty decent with a win at EPL Masters III just a few weeks ago. They’re a young roster with the potential to stand up against the big dogs.  
 We haven’t really seen Xtreme Gaming in a while, which is why I’ve put them relatively low on the list. Still, they have incredibly experienced players and the element of surprise, so maybe they’ll impress.  
 Image via Valve / The International 
 An underrated team I’ve really been digging is LEGION. They played a very solid tournament at 1win Essence III, making it relatively deep into the tournament. Their mid-laner Copy has been doing God’s work for the team, so I’m excited to watch him play again.  
 Aside from these squads, I wouldn’t be surprised to see any of 1win Team, Astra Invicta, and OG performing well at this event, as they certainly have the potential to do some great things.
